messages:
support-oncall: FYI ACME hit a p99 latency spike ~02:14-02:20 UTC. Their dashboard shows a bunch of GPU OOMs and then p99 went from 220ms -> 2.4s. Putting notes here while I dig.
maria: Ack — do we have the worker IDs / pool? can you paste the sampler logs or link to the traces?
support-oncall: pool-9 (g5xlarge-9). Logs: seeing repeated allocator errors and slab compaction kicks. snippet:
```
[02:14:12] allocator: cannot allocate 2300MB: OOM
[02:14:13] slab_compact: started, reclaimed 0MB
[02:14:14] kv_store: entries=3.8M growth=+120k/min
[02:14:15] p99=2400ms p95=420ms
```
devon: kv growth looks notable. Any recent changes to per-tenant cache limits or long-context customers? eli: last night we rolled a pilot that bumped kv.max_entries from 2M -> 4M for some tenants (internal config id: cfg/kv-raise-2026-03). Could be related.
maria: If kv growth is unbounded it fragments GPU memory (slab churn). Two quick mitigations: 1) throttle tenant, 2) force a worker drain on impacted nodes to let allocators compact on restart.
support-oncall: I'm running a targeted throttle now for tenant acme-corp via rate-limit route (weight down to 30%). Also filing drain for the 3 workers: worker-9-a/b/c. deploy-bot: Initiating graceful drain for worker-9-a. ETA ~40s.
eli: For next steps we should (A) set temporary slab_compact aggressiveness and (B) set kv.max_entries back to 2M until we understand workload shape. Suggested quick flags:
```
allocator.slab_compact_threshold=0.45
allocator.max_slab_free_ratio=0.25
kv.max_entries=2000000
```
maria: +1 on reverting cfg/kv-raise-2026-03 for the cohort. Also add a short-lived eviction policy: kv.eviction.target_percent=70 to force earlier evicts
devon: I can push the config rollback and the allocator flags to pool-9 now. Are we doing this as a feature-flag change or direct agent config?
support-oncall: Do direct cluster config patch (circumvent rollout) — need speed. Please patch and signal when done.
devon: Patching now. Commands I ran:
```
kubectl -n inference set env daemonset/runtime allocator.slab_compact_threshold=0.45
kubectl patch configmap kv-config -p '{"data":{"max_entries":"2000000","eviction_target_percent":"70"}}'
```
infra-bot: Patch applied to 3/3 nodes in pool-9. Restart scheduled for rolling-restart-of-runtime pods.
support-oncall: After patch and rolling restart p99 dropped back to ~310ms within 4 minutes. ACME reports improvements. Logs show fewer OOMs and compaction reclaimed some free slabs:
```
[02:18:03] slab_compact: started, reclaimed 1.2GB
[02:18:07] allocator: allocation success
[02:18:10] kv_store: entries=2.05M growth=+2k/min
[02:18:15] p99=320ms p95=95ms
```
maria: Nice — follow-ups: open a postmortem with root cause (config change + workload shape), add guardrails to prevent auto increase of kv.max_entries without traffic profile checks, and add an alert on kv.entry_growth_rate > 50k/min per pool.
eli: Also propose a perf-test that simulates long-context streaming and heavy KV churn to validate future kv increases.
support-oncall: Will create a short runbook for oncall: 1) check kv growth, 2) throttle tenant, 3) revert kv.max_entries, 4) set slab_compact flags, 5) drain/restart nodes. Tagging @maria for postmortem lead. :white_check_mark:
